messages:
opsbot: Pager: unusual outbound S3 activity from staging-logs-prod-2. ~1.8k PUTs/min. Possible sensitive payloads. Correlation id: c9f3a2. https://incidents/redwood/6478901234 :rotating_light:

sanjay (oncall): taking this. pulling traces and blocking egress at edge ACLs now. which service account owns that bucket?

patrick (eng-sre): looks like svcacct: staging-log-forwarder (k8s ns=staging). I see flurry from pod staging-forwarder-7f9c in us-east-1a. attaching recent container logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T02:01:12Z PUT /staging-logs-prod-2/2026-03-17/evt-... 200 size=12kb token=ya29.***
2026-03-17T02:01:13Z PUT /staging-logs-prod-2/... token=AKIA***
```

maria (security): ack. treat as suspected credential exposure. immediate steps: 1) block egress from the pod to S3, 2) revoke/rotate keys for staging-log-forwarder, 3) snapshot pod for forensics, 4) check whether customer identifiers are present and scope impact.

patrick (eng-sre): running firewall block: `kubectl annotate node us-east-1a no-egress=true` then `iptables -I OUTPUT -d s3.amazonaws.com -j DROP` on node; doing now.

sanjay (oncall): block applied, PUTs dropped. traffic rate back to baseline. starting snapshot: `kubectl cp staging-logs-prod-2:/var/log/forwarder /tmp/forensics-6478901234`

patrick (eng-sre): rotation script queued. command we will run (one-line):
```bash
./tools/rotate-service-keys.sh --svc staging-log-forwarder --env staging --notify kms
```
Estimated 3 min to complete with short tailing downtime for forwarder.

maria (security): also ask infra to create short-lived deny rule at cloud egress to prevent cross-region exfil while rotation happens. sending ACL change to infra-runbook.

lucy (support): I can draft a cautious customer note if we confirm any customer identifiers. can we get a quick impact callout?

patrick (eng-sre): grep of latest files: found three object keys containing customer ids: cust-712, cust-88, cust-115. payloads look like trace dumps and some request headers. no clear full PII yet but tokens / API keys present in two files.

maria (security): classification: suspected leaked tokens + headers. customer impact: potential token exposure for three customers; data-in-files include request metadata and partial traces. escalate legal.

kevin (customer-success): flagged custodians for cust-88 and cust-115, prepping outreach language. prefer to confirm rotations first before external notice.

patrick (eng-sre): rotation complete: new creds issued and applied to staging-forwarder. old keys revoked in IAM at 6478901401. forwarding service restarted and backfilling to a secure bucket.

maria (security): forensic snapshot uploaded to secure-store s3://forensics/6478901234.tar.gz. saved hashes and chain-of-custody in case legal needs them.

sanjay (oncall): handing off monitoring to lucy (night oncall). lucy please watch for reattempts and any lateral egress. set pager threshold to 50 PUTs/min for this bucket.

lucy (support): ack, taking over. will run hourly checks and escalate if anything pops. draft customer note prepared, waiting on legal.

maria (security): next actions: 1) legal + privacy notified, 2) run wider grep across prod/staging buckets for token patterns, 3) review RBAC that allowed staging-forwarder to write customer logs. I'll open follow-up ticket SEC-2026-103.

kevin (customer-success): will be on standby for customer comms; prefer coordinated message after legal review.

opsbot: Incident updated: status -> contained. owner -> lucy (support). link: https://incidents/redwood/6478901234/updates

sanjay (oncall): nice work team. documenting steps in the incident playbook and assigning postmortem.

maria (security): note: rotate any long-lived tokens found in the artifacts for the three customers as precaution; request permission from customers via kevin before rotating customer-managed keys.

lucy (support): taking the handoff. will keep channel updated every hour until all legal/customer steps are complete. :white_check_mark:
